daily_brief: A coordinated cyberattack targeting supermarket refrigeration systems spread across six European countries overnight, marking a significant escalation from a similar incident that struck France last month [BBC], [France 24], [Al Jazeera]. The attacks, which caused temperatures to spike in freezers across Belgium, Luxembourg, Sweden, Ireland, the Netherlands, and Estonia, have resulted in millions of euros in food losses and underscore growing vulnerabilities in critical infrastructure. Meanwhile, as the US midterm elections approach on Tuesday, voters are weighing economic anxieties against broader geopolitical concerns [RFI], [France 24], with Republican strongholds showing signs of weakness amid inflation pressures. In Sudan, the anniversary of the fall of El Fasher has prompted UK sanctions against 15 military commanders implicated in sexual violence [The Guardian], while the UAE's nomination of diplomat Lana Nusseibeh for UN Secretary-General faces opposition from Sudanese diaspora groups citing concerns over the country's alleged support for the RSF [The Guardian]. Iran has signaled flexibility in negotiations with the US over the Strait of Hormuz, proposing a two-day timeline to restore maritime security if its conditions are met [The Hindu], [Al Jazeera]. Cost-of-living protests continue across Europe, with French authorities launching an attempted murder investigation after a Molotov cocktail attack on police [BBC], [RFI].

top_stories.headline: Coordinated Cyberattack Hits Supermarket Refrigeration Systems Across Six European Countries
bullets: Overnight temperature spikes affected refrigerators and freezers in approximately 40 Delhaize stores in Belgium and Luxembourg, plus stores in Sweden, Ireland, the Netherlands, and Estonia
The attack method—switching evaporators to defrost mode—mirrors the technique used in October's cyberattack on hundreds of French supermarkets that caused fires and food losses
Sabcobel CEO confirmed the incident as a cyberattack and said affected units require physical modifications, not just software updates, to address the vulnerability
Swedish cybersecurity authorities confirmed they are responding to multiple incidents and had previously warned about exposed operational technology devices requiring patches

North Carolina, traditionally a Republican stronghold, shows vulnerability due to agricultural sector impacts from inflation
President Trump's unpopularity is reportedly affecting Republican candidates across multiple states
Online betting companies are investing heavily in state elections, seeing an opportunity to shape future gambling regulations

top_stories.headline: UK Sanctions 15 Sudanese Military Commanders on Anniversary of El Fasher Massacre
bullets: British government imposed travel bans and asset freezes on commanders from both the RSF and Sudanese Armed Forces suspected of sexual violence during the siege of El Fasher
Up to 10,000 civilians were killed over two days when the RSF captured El Fasher in October 2025, with another 40,000 still unaccounted for
El Fasher's population has dropped from over 1 million to fewer than 70,000 remaining residents
The sanctions come as UAE diplomat Lana Nusseibeh's candidacy for UN Secretary-General faces opposition from Sudanese diaspora and human rights groups over the UAE's alleged support for the RSF

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.framing_note: Provided detailed coverage of both the sanctions and opposition to Nusseibeh's UN candidacy

sources.framing_note: Focused on conditions in El Fasher one year after the fall

top_stories.headline: Iran Signals Flexibility on Hormuz Strait, Proposes Two-Day Timeline for Reopening
bullets: Iran's Foreign Ministry said it is considering a two-day plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz if US conditions are met, shortened from a previous seven-day proposal
Qatar is facilitating indirect talks between Tehran and Washington based on Iran's seven-step peace plan
Iranian demands include ending the West Asia war, unfreezing Iranian assets, lifting oil sanctions, and ending the US naval blockade
China's Foreign Minister met with Iranian officials in Beijing, pushing for dialogue over military solutions and expressing support for Iran's sovereignty

top_stories.headline: France Launches Attempted Murder Probe After Molotov Cocktail Sets Officer Ablaze During Protests
bullets: Paris prosecutors opened an investigation for attempted murder of persons vested with public authority after petrol bombs were thrown at police during Saturday's protests
Images showed a homemade incendiary device exploding at an officer's feet, causing second-degree burns to his ankle and minor hand injuries
Hundreds of thousands participated in largely peaceful demonstrations across France protesting high living costs and poor public services, with over 770 arrests made Saturday
Student groups have announced plans to resume high school blockades starting Monday despite President Macron calling for calm return to classes
